title: Bread for the Winter
text: A boy comes up the hill from {village} with a cracked bowl. The low fields flooded, and the families below the church have eaten their seed. They ask the house for bread, and say they will remember it.

choices.label: Send bread down from the granary
choices.chronicle: {When}, the house sent bread down to {village}, and the families there said so at the church door.

choices.label: Tell the boy the house has none to spare
choices.chronicle: {When}, the boy went back down the hill with an empty bowl, and {village} remembered it.

title: A Wall That Moved
text: Two families of {village} have come up with a witness each, over a stone wall that stood in one place yesterday and in another this morning. Both want the house to say whose the wall is.

choices.label: Go down and settle it between them

success.chronicle: {When}, the abbot walked the line with both families and set the wall where both could agree, and {village} went home talking of it.

failure.chronicle: {When}, neither family would give way, and the abbot went back up the hill with the quarrel still open.

choices.label: Say the wall belongs to the house and let no one touch it
choices.chronicle: {When}, the house claimed the wall, and {village} said nothing, and did not forget.

title: A Fever Below the Church
text: A child of {village} has a fever that will not break, and the mother has come up the hill on foot to ask for the infirmary's medicine.

choices.label: Send the medicine down
choices.chronicle: {When}, the house sent medicine down to {village}, and the child who had been given up for dead was carried up the hill a week later to say thank you.

choices.label: Send a brother down to pray with the family
choices.chronicle: {When}, a brother went down to {village} to pray with the family, and came back without the medicine.

choices.label: Say the house has no medicine to spare
choices.chronicle: {When}, the mother went down the hill without the medicine, and {village} counted the house's words.

title: Torches at the Gate
text: A crowd comes up the road from {village} after dark, with torches. A rumour has reached them that the house keeps grain it will not share, and they want to see the granary.

choices.label: Open the granary and show them
choices.chronicle: {When}, the granary was opened to the crowd from {village}. They went down again with what they could carry, and with less anger.

choices.label: Bar the gate and keep the bell ringing
choices.chronicle: {When}, the gate was barred, and the crowd from {village} stood under the wall until dawn, and went home angry.

title: Banns Read at Mass
text: A wedding is to be made in {village}. The families ask the house to read the banns and to feed the guests after. The house has a claim on the village now, and they know it.

choices.label: Read the banns and feed the guests
choices.chronicle: {When}, the banns were read in the chapel, and the wedding feast in {village} was given from the house's stores.

choices.label: Read the banns and ask for a prayer only
choices.chronicle: {When}, the banns were read, and the wedding in {village} went ahead without a feast.

title: A Sheaf Kept Back
text: When the tithe carts came up from {village} this season, the families sent word that they would keep back a sheaf in ten until the house mends the bridge over the stream.

choices.label: Press them for the full tithe
choices.chronicle: {When}, the full tithe came up from {village}, and was counted at the gate without a word.

choices.label: Let them keep it, and say nothing
choices.chronicle: {When}, the house let {village} keep its sheaf, and the carts went down light.
